extraction.title: Enhance embed URL handling and validation system
extraction.head: embed-url-handling-post

greptile.text: Summarizes the PR as an embedding system for importing RSS/ATOM content into Discourse, covering TopicEmbed, EmbedController, TopicRetriever, PollFeed, embed.js, and site settings. Warns of multiple critical security issues (unsafe open() HTTP calls, weak origin validation in JavaScript, possible XSS from unescaped content, SSRF vectors) and gives a confidence score of 1/5.
Adding force: true makes the migration destructive, since it can drop and recreate an existing table and lose production data. Suggests removing force: true.
Flags the unusual 'end if' closing tag as a syntax issue; suggests changing it to a plain end.
Says open() is deprecated and creates command injection and SSRF risks. Suggests replacing it with Net::HTTP.get_response(URI(url)).body.
The require_dependency path is wrong; it should be 'jobs/scheduled/poll_feed', not 'jobs/regular/process_post'.
URL validation is insufficient and allows access to internal services such as localhost and 192.168.x.x. Asks for proper SSRF protection.
ensure_embeddable host check can be bypassed when request.referer is nil, because the '|| ""' fallback yields a nil host that could match a nil embeddable_host.
postMessageReceived uses indexOf on the origin, which allows subdomain attacks. Suggests exact origin matching against a normalized Discourse URL.
Setting X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL permits embedding from any domain, which could enable clickjacking from malicious sites.
Using open() on SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validation allows SSRF and local file access. Suggests URI parsing, an http/https scheme check, and Net::HTTP with a success check.
Style nit: suggests find_by(id: args[:user_id]) instead of where(...).first.
